facts.fact: Businessday, citing Project BRIDGE's implementation documents, says the programme requires more than 400 local government headquarters to be connected and more than 59,000 public institutions, government offices among them, linked by 2030, on a schedule of 17,500 km of fibre in the first year, 25,000 km in each of 2028 and 2029 and 22,500 km in 2030; the document's own date is used.

Businessday reports Project BRIDGE's financing appraised at US$1.6bn: US$500m from the World Bank's IDA, US$200m from the African Development Bank, US$100m from the EBRD, US$100m from BADEA and US$1.1bn expected from private and commercial investors, with no domestic budget line stated; the document's own date is used.

Businessday reports that private investors are expected to own 51 to 75 per cent of the special purpose vehicle that will build Project BRIDGE, leaving the Federal Government a minority of 25 to 49 per cent; the vehicle was still to be established and the document's own date is used.

The communications minister said on 4 August 2026 that resource mobilisation and contractual processes for the 90,000 km fibre network were complete and that laying would start within weeks; no fibre had been laid and no local government headquarters is said to be connected.

systems.owner: a special purpose vehicle, 51 to 75 per cent private and 25 to 49 per cent Federal Government, not yet established
systems.tiers: 90,000 km of open-access wholesale fibre in six construction zones; more than 400 local government headquarters to be connected; more than 59,000 public institutions including schools, hospitals and government offices by 2030; high-capacity connectivity to all 774 local government areas, as the regulator puts it

note: Classed connection here only because this account says local government headquarters are to be connected; it does not say whether that means the council's office or the headquarters town, and nothing was built at the date.
